plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 adipose samples (6 treated, 6 control), raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), with sex and age recorded per sample and no batch structure. The question has two parts. First, quantify how much of the per-gene expression variance is attributable to condition, sex, and age before any group test is run, using variancePartition on voom log-CPM with precision weights (condition and sex as random effects, age as a continuous fixed effect), so the design choice for the DE model is evidence-based rather than assumed. Second, test treated vs control for differential expression with DESeq2 (median-of-ratios normalization, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH-FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05), adjusting for sex and age as fixed-effect covariates in the design since both were measured and could confound the comparison. Genes are filtered to >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smallest group size) before the test. The ranked DE statistic then feeds a preranked fgsea enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1) and Reactome (current) gene sets. A combined report ties the variance-partition diagnostic to the DE and enrichment results, with all required diagnostics (PCA/sample-distance QC, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, session info, package and gene-set-collection versions).
